---
title: "API reference"
---

All classes and functions are in the `CmdStan` namespace. Standalone functions keep CmdStanR's snake_case names. Methods and their parameters are camelCase, so CmdStanR's `fit$output_files()` is `$fit->outputFiles()`, and [Compatibility](compatibility.qmd#method-names) maps every renamed method. CmdStan's option names are unchanged.

Inference methods accept PHP named arguments or one associative options array, and they reject unknown options. An option left out or set to `null` uses the installed CmdStan's default.

## Functions

### Models and Stan files

| Function | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `cmdstan_model(stanFile: null, exeFile: null, quiet: true, dir: null, pedantic: false, includePaths: null, userHeader: null, cppOptions: null, stancOptions: null, forceRecompile: null)` | A `CmdStanModel`, compiled or reusing an up-to-date executable |
| `compile_stan_file(stanFile, ...)` | The executable path, compiled with `cmdstan_model()`'s build arguments but without a model object |
| `check_syntax_stan_file(stanFile, includePaths: null, pedantic: false, stancOptions: [], quiet: false)` | `true`, or an exception for invalid Stan |
| `format_stan_file(stanFile, includePaths: null, overwriteFile: false, canonicalize: false, backup: true, maxLineLength: null, quiet: false)` | The formatted program. `overwriteFile` rewrites the file and keeps a `.bak-YYYYMMDDHHMMSS` copy unless `backup: false`. |
| `variables_stan_file(stanFile, includePaths: null)` | The program's declarations, without compiling |
| `print_stan_file(stanFile, lineNumbers: null)` | Prints the program |
| `stan_build_info(exeFile)` | How an executable was built, from its build record and what it reports about itself |
| `write_stan_file(code, file: null, dir: null, basename: null, forceOverwrite: false, hashSalt: '')` | The path of `model_<hash>.stan`, or of `basename`. An identical existing file is left untouched. |

### CmdStan installation

| Function | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `install_cmdstan(version: null, dir: null, cores: null, timeout: null, overwrite: false, releaseUrl: null, releaseFile: null, cppOptions: [], checkToolchain: true, copyMakeLocal: null)` | Downloads or unpacks a release, builds it, and selects it. See [Installation](installation.qmd#install-cmdstan). |
| `set_cmdstan_path(path)`, `cmdstan_path()` | Selects or returns the CmdStan installation |
| `cmdstan_version()` | The selected CmdStan's version |
| `check_cmdstan_toolchain()` | Paths and versions of make, CmdStan's C++ compiler, and stanc. Throws when make or the compiler is missing. A successful check does not prove that a compilation will succeed. |
| `cmdstan_make_local(dir: null, cppOptions: [], append: true)` | Reads or writes CmdStan's `make/local` |
| `rebuild_cmdstan(cores: null, timeout: null)` | Cleans and rebuilds the selected CmdStan |

CmdStan 2.37 is the oldest supported release, as in CmdStanR 1.0. `set_cmdstan_path()` refuses an older installation, discovery skips one, and `install_cmdstan()` rejects older versions. CI tests 2.37 and 2.40. Options added in newer CmdStan releases fail on older ones with CmdStan's error message.

### Data and CSV files

| Function | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `write_stan_json(data, file, alwaysDecimal: false, variables: null)` | Writes data, initial values, or a metric as JSON. `data` may be an array, a `StanData`, or a table. With `variables` (stanc's declarations, such as `$model->variables()['data']`), `int` variables are written as integers and tuples as Stan's `{"1": ..., "2": ...}` objects. |
| `read_cmdstan_csv(files)` | A fit from one or more CmdStan CSV files (`.csv`, `.csv.gz`, or `.csv.bz2`) |
| `as_cmdstan_fit(files, variables: null, checkDiagnostics: true, format: null)` | The same, reading only `variables` and with `format` as the fit's default draws format |
| `read_cmdstan_csv_list(files, variables: null, samplerDiagnostics: null, format: null)` | CmdStanR's `read_cmdstan_csv()` list shape |
| `draws_to_csv(chains, dir)` | Writes `[chain][iteration][variable]` draw rows to one CSV file per chain |

Data arrays are named PHP arrays at the top level, with lists for Stan arrays, vectors, and matrices:

- Matrices are lists of rows, with no column-major conversion. Booleans become 0 and 1, complex numbers are `[re, im]` pairs, and a tuple is a list of its elements. Empty top-level data becomes `{}`.
- Missing values, strings, objects, nonfinite numbers, sparse indices, invalid variable names, and ragged arrays are rejected, and the error names the variable.
- The fitting methods write data with the model's declarations. Every declared data variable is required, `int` variables are written as integers (a non-integer is truncated with a warning), and a single value for a one-dimensional array becomes a one-element array.

### Figures and examples

| Function | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `mcmc_trace`, `mcmc_hist`, `mcmc_dens`, `mcmc_dens_overlay`, `mcmc_intervals`, `mcmc_rank_hist`, `mcmc_scatter`, `mcmc_acf`, `pareto_k_plot` | A `Figure`, named after its bayesplot or loo counterpart. See [Figures](figures.qmd). |
| `cmdstanr_example(example: 'logistic', method: 'sample', ...options)` | A fit of the `logistic`, `schools`, or `schools_ncp` example |
| `print_example_program(example)` | Prints an example's Stan program |

`num_threads()` remains as a deprecated CmdStanR name. CmdStanR 1.0 removed `read_sample_csv()` and `write_stan_tempfile()`, and this package does not have them.

### Global options

`options(set: [])` sets options and returns their previous values, and `cmdstan_option(name, default: null)` reads one. A `null` value unsets an option, and unknown names and values of the wrong type throw.

| Option | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `cmdstanr_output_dir` | Default `output_dir` |
| `cmdstanr_write_stan_file_dir` | Default directory for `write_stan_file()` |
| `cmdstanr_force_recompile` | Default `forceRecompile` |
| `cmdstanr_draws_format` | Default draws format: `draws_array`, `draws_matrix`, `draws_df`, or `draws_list` |
| `cmdstanr_compress` | Default `compress`: `'none'`, `'gzip'`, or `'bzip2'` |
| `cmdstanr_progress_bar` | Default `show_progress_bar` for `sample()` |
| `cmdstanr_save_metric` | Default `save_metric` for `sample()` |
| `cmdstanr_save_config` | Default `save_cmdstan_config` |
| `cmdstanr_verbose` | Reports whether and why a model compiles |
| `cmdstanr_warn_inits` | Warns when initial values cover only some parameters, and passes on warnings from initializing with a fit. On by default. |
| `cmdstanr_max_rows` | Variables printed by `print()` (default 10) |
| `cmdstanr_print_line_numbers` | Default `lineNumbers` for `print_stan_file()` and `print()` |
| `mc.cores` | Default `parallel_chains` and installer core count |
| `cmdstanphp_example_dir` | Directory for compiled examples |
| `cmdstanr_no_ver_check`, `cmdstanr_spinner` | Accepted and ignored |

## Models {#model-methods}

`cmdstan_model()` and `new CmdStanModel()` take the same arguments and compile the model, or reuse an up-to-date executable, before they return.

- Give `stanFile`, whose executable goes beside it or in `dir`, or `exeFile` alone to use an existing executable. A model from `exeFile` alone refuses the build arguments, because there is nothing to build.
- `cppOptions` are named make variables, such as `['STAN_THREADS' => true]`. Names are uppercased, and `false` turns an option off even when `make/local` turns it on. Unnamed entries and values containing command expansions or shell metacharacters are rejected. Use `cmdstan_make_local()` for other make lines.
- `stancOptions` take flags and values, such as `['O1', 'canonicalize' => 'deprecations', 'max-line-length' => 78]`. Flags with their own argument are rejected: use `includePaths`, `pedantic`, `userHeader`, or `cppOptions: ['STAN_OPENCL' => true]`.
- `quiet: false`, or the `cmdstanr_verbose` option, reports whether and why the model compiles. `forceRecompile: true` rebuilds anyway.

[Compiling models](compiling.qmd) covers when a model is rebuilt, `StaleExecutableException`, and concurrent builds.

### Inspecting a model

| Method | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `stanFile()`, `exeFile()`, `hppFile()` | Paths. `hppFile()` writes the generated C++ to a temporary file on first use. |
| `code()` | The program as it was when the model was created |
| `variables()` | The `data`, `parameters`, `transformed_parameters`, and `generated_quantities` declarations, from stanc |
| `modelName()`, `hasStanFile()`, `includePaths()`, `userHeader()`, `stancOptions()` | The model's identity and recorded build settings |
| `cppOptions()` | Make variables and values, so `['stan_threads' => true]` comes back as `['STAN_THREADS' => 'true']` |
| `cmdstanVersion()` | The CmdStan version that built the executable |
| `reportedFeatures()` | What the executable reports: `stan_threads`, `stan_mpi`, `stan_opencl`, `stan_no_range_checks`, and `stan_version` |
| `buildInfo()` | The build record and the reported features, as `stan_build_info()` returns them |
| `isCurrent()` | `false` when the executable is out of date |
| `cmdstanDefaults(method: 'sample')` | CmdStan's default values for `sample`, `optimize`, `variational`, `pathfinder`, or `laplace`, under this package's option names |
| `print(lineNumbers: null)`, `saveHppFile(dir)` | Prints the program, or copies the generated header |
| `format(overwriteFile: false, canonicalize: false, backup: true, maxLineLength: null, quiet: false)` | The formatted program. Create the model again to use a rewritten file. |
| `checkSyntax(pedantic: false, includePaths: null, stancOptions: [], quiet: false)` | `true`, or an exception for invalid Stan |
| `exposeFunctions(timeout: null, quiet: false)`, `functions()` | The model's user-defined functions as a `StanFunctions` object |

`code()` and `hppFile()` are `null` for a model from `exeFile` alone.

### Running a model

| Method | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `sample()`, `sampleMpi()` | `CmdStanMCMC` |
| `optimize()` | `CmdStanMLE` |
| `variational()` | `CmdStanVB` |
| `pathfinder()` | `CmdStanPathfinder` |
| `laplace()` | `CmdStanLaplace` |
| `generateQuantities(fittedParams, ...)` | `CmdStanGQ` |
| `diagnose()` | `CmdStanDiagnose` |
| `logProb()` | `CmdStanFit` |

### Shared options

| Option | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `data` | An array, a JSON file, a `StanData`, or a [table](#data-in) | None |
| `seed` | Random seed | Chosen by CmdStan |
| `init` | Initial values: a radius, values, files, a callable, or a fit. See [initial values](mcmc.qmd#initial-values). | CmdStan's radius of 2 |
| `refresh` | Iterations between progress lines | CmdStan's |
| `output_dir` | Directory for output files | The `cmdstanr_output_dir` option, else a new temporary directory |
| `output_basename` | File name prefix: letters, numbers, dots, underscores, and hyphens. Files are then named `<output_basename>-<id>.csv`. | `<model>-<YYYYmmddHHMM>`, with a random suffix after the chain id |
| `sig_figs` | Significant figures in the CSV output, 1 to 18 | CmdStan's |
| `compress` | `'none'`, `'gzip'`, or `'bzip2'` for the output and latent-dynamics CSV files. Not for `diagnose()` or `logProb()`. | The `cmdstanr_compress` option |
| `opencl_ids` | OpenCL platform and device IDs. Needs an OpenCL build. | None |
| `save_cmdstan_config` | Writes CmdStan's configuration JSON beside the CSV files | The `cmdstanr_save_config` option |
| `show_messages`, `show_exceptions` | Print CmdStan's standard output and standard error | `true`, and `show_exceptions` follows `show_messages` |
| `timeout` | Seconds allowed per process | None |

Threads are `threads_per_chain` for `sample()` and `generateQuantities()`, and `threads` for `optimize()`, `variational()`, `pathfinder()`, and `laplace()`. `pathfinder()` still accepts `num_threads` with an `E_USER_DEPRECATED` notice. Asking for more than one thread from an executable built without threading is an error.

CmdStanR 1.0's removed names are unknown options here too: `sample()`'s `cores`, `num_cores`, `num_chains`, `num_warmup`, `num_samples`, `max_depth`, `stepsize`, `save_extra_diagnostics`, and `validate_csv`, and `jacobian_adjustment`.

### Method-specific options

| Method | Options |
| --- | --- |
| `sample()` | `threads_per_chain`, `save_latent_dynamics`, `show_progress_bar`, `chains` (default 4), `parallel_chains` (default: the `mc.cores` option, else 1), `chain_ids`, `iter_warmup`, `iter_sampling`, `save_warmup`, `thin`, `max_treedepth`, `adapt_engaged`, `adapt_delta`, `step_size`, `metric`, `metric_file`, `inv_metric`, `init_buffer`, `term_buffer`, `window`, `fixed_param`, `save_metric`, `diagnostics`. See [MCMC sampling](mcmc.qmd). |
| `optimize()` | `threads`, `algorithm`, `jacobian`, `init_alpha`, `iter`, `tol_obj`, `tol_rel_obj`, `tol_grad`, `tol_rel_grad`, `tol_param`, `history_size`, `save_iterations` |
| `variational()` | `threads`, `save_latent_dynamics`, `algorithm`, `iter`, `grad_samples`, `elbo_samples`, `eta`, `adapt_engaged`, `adapt_iter`, `tol_rel_obj`, `eval_elbo`, `draws` (CmdStan's `output_samples`) |
| `pathfinder()` | `threads`, `init_alpha`, `tol_obj`, `tol_rel_obj`, `tol_grad`, `tol_rel_grad`, `tol_param`, `history_size`, `single_path_draws`, `draws`, `num_paths`, `max_lbfgs_iters`, `num_elbo_draws`, `save_single_paths`, `psis_resample`, `calculate_lp` |
| `laplace()` | `threads`, `mode`, `opt_args`, `jacobian` (default true), `draws`, `calculate_lp` |
| `generateQuantities()` | `fittedParams` (required: a fit, a CSV file name, or a list of them), `threads_per_chain`, `parallel_chains` |
| `diagnose()` | `epsilon` and `error`, for the finite-difference gradient check |
| `logProb()` | Exactly one of `unconstrained_params` and `constrained_params`, and `jacobian` |

`save_latent_dynamics` writes auxiliary diagnostic CSV files.

`sampleMpi(mpiCmd: 'mpiexec', mpiArgs: [], ...options)` takes the sampling options, defaults to one chain, and runs chains one after another. An associative argument such as `['n' => 4]` becomes `-n 4`, and a list is passed as literal arguments. Compile with `['STAN_MPI' => true, 'CXX' => 'mpicxx', 'TBB_CXX_TYPE' => 'gcc']` and install an MPI runtime. The launch command is unit-tested, but no run on a real MPI cluster has been tested.

## Fits {#fit-methods}

[Draws, summaries, and saving fits](draws.qmd) explains formats, summaries, and saving.

### Draws and summaries

| Method | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `draws(variables: null, format: null, incWarmup: false)` | Draws in `draws_array`, `draws_matrix`, `draws_df`, `draws_list`, or `draws_rvars` format |
| `samplerDiagnostics(format: null, incWarmup: false)` | Sampler columns ending in `__`, except `lp__` |
| `summary(variables: null, probs: [0.05, 0.95], measures: [])` | One row per variable |
| `drawsColumns(variables: null, incWarmup: false)`, `summaryColumns(...)` | The same as column arrays. See [data frames](#draws-and-summaries-out). |
| `drawsTable(...)`, `summaryTable(...)` | The same as a `Phibble\DataFrame` |
| `print(variables: null, maxRows: null)` | Prints summary JSON for at most `cmdstanr_max_rows` variables |
| `lp()` | `lp__` by iteration and chain |
| `cmdstanSummary()` | CmdStan's `stansummary` text |

A fit reads its CSV metadata and checks every row when it is created, then reads only the columns that `draws()`, `summary()`, and the diagnostics use, as packed doubles. Each read of new columns passes over the files again, so request variables together. Until `materialize()`, the fit needs its CSV files.

### Diagnostics and run information

| Method | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `diagnosticSummary()` | Per-chain `num_divergent`, `num_max_treedepth`, and `ebfmi` |
| `checkDiagnostics(checks: ['divergences', 'treedepth', 'ebfmi'])`, `diagnosticWarnings()` | Runs the checks, or returns their messages |
| `cmdstanDiagnose()` | The text from CmdStan's `diagnose` utility |
| `metadata()`, `chainMetadata()` | CSV metadata, merged or per chain |
| `variables()`, `numChains()`, `numDrawsSampling()`, `numDrawsWarmup()`, `numProcs()` | Counts and names from the CSV files |
| `stepSize()`, `invMetric(matrix: true)` | Adaptation results, one per chain |
| `time()` | Warmup, sampling, and total time per chain, when available |
| `init()` | The initial values each process used |
| `output()`, `returnCodes()`, `command()` | Console output, exit status, and command line of each process. Imported fits have none of these. `command()` leaves out `STAN_NUM_THREADS` and an MPI launcher. |
| `code()` | The Stan program. Imported fits have none. |

### Files and saving

| Method | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `outputFiles()`, `latentDynamicsFiles()`, `profileFiles()` | File paths. The latent-dynamics and profile accessors throw when there are no such files. `includeFailed` is accepted for CmdStanR compatibility. |
| `profiles()` | Parsed profiling data |
| `dataFile()`, `configFiles()`, `metricFiles()` | Paths. An imported fit uses the data file recorded in the CSV when it still exists. |
| `cmdstanConfig()`, `metric()` | The decoded configuration and metric JSON |
| `saveOutputFiles()`, `saveLatentDynamicsFiles()`, `saveProfileFiles()`, `saveDataFile()`, `saveConfigFiles()`, `saveMetricFiles()` | Saved paths. Each takes `dir: '.', basename: null, timestamp: true, random: true`, and the first two also take `compress`. |
| `materialize()` | Reads the draws, initial values, and profiles into memory |
| `saveObject(file)` | Materializes and serializes the fit, with MCMC summary statistics |

### Model methods

These need PHP's FFI extension. The first call compiles a shared library for the fit's model and data, and `initModelMethods(data: null, seed: 1, verbose: false, quiet: false, model: null)` does this explicitly. `data` binds other data, for example when a reloaded fit's data file is gone, and `dataFile()` then points to it. Imported CSV fits must pass `model:`, and a model from `exeFile` alone has no program to build them from. See [Log density and model methods](log-density.qmd).

| Method | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `logProb(unconstrainedVariables, jacobian: true)` | The log density, with constants dropped |
| `gradLogProb(...)` | `['log_prob' => float, 'gradient' => list]` |
| `hessian(...)` | `['log_prob' => float, 'grad_log_prob' => list, 'hessian' => rows]` |
| `unconstrainVariables(variables)` | A flat unconstrained list from parameter values keyed by name, shaped as `constrainVariables()` returns them |
| `unconstrainDraws(files: null, draws: null, format: null, incWarmup: false)` | The fit's draws, other CSV files, or `draws_df` rows on the unconstrained scale |
| `constrainVariables(unconstrainedVariables, transformedParameters: true, generatedQuantities: true)` | Variables keyed by name as nested arrays, with tuples as lists and complex values as `[re, im]` |
| `exposeFunctions(timeout: null)`, `functions()` | The model's user-defined functions |

`CmdStan\ModelMethods` and `CmdStan\StanFunctions` can also be used directly with a Stan file.

| Fit | Methods |

| `CmdStanMCMC` | `loo(variables: 'log_lik', rEff: false, momentMatch: false, maxIters: 30, kThreshold: null, split: true, cov: true)` and `waic(variables: 'log_lik')`. See [LOO and WAIC](loo.qmd). |
| `CmdStanMLE` | `mle()` and `optimizedParams()` (the estimates without `lp__`), and `lp()`. Its `summary()` returns `variable` and `estimate` rows. |
| `CmdStanVB` | `variationalMean()`, and `lpApprox()`, the approximation's log density at each draw |
| `CmdStanLaplace` | `mode()` and `lpApprox()` |
| `CmdStanPathfinder` | `lpApprox()`, and `singlePathFiles()`, `singlePathJsonFiles()`, `singlePathFits()`, and `singlePathDiagnostics()` with `save_single_paths: true`. Its variables include `lp_approx__` and `path__`. |
| `CmdStanGQ` | `fittedParamsFiles()` |
| `CmdStanDiagnose` | `gradients()`, the gradient check's console output |

## Data frames and the phpstats family

CmdStanPHP works with the [phpstats family](#part-of-the-phpstats-family) without depending on it. phibble is detected by method and class names. The `phit` extension is detected by function name.

### Data in

Every `data` argument (`sample()`, `sampleMpi()`, `optimize()`, `variational()`, `pathfinder()`, `laplace()`, `generateQuantities()`, `diagnose()`, and `logProb()`) and `write_stan_json()` accept a plain array, a JSON file, a `CmdStan\StanData`, or a table. A table is any object with `toModelData()` or `toColumns()`, such as a [phibble](https://github.com/phpstats/phibble) `Phibble\DataFrame`. `toModelData()` is used when both exist. `StanData::fromTable($table, addN: true)` performs the same conversion and keeps the factor labels.

| Column | Stan data |
| --- | --- |
| int or float | The list of values, unchanged |
| bool | 0/1 integers |
| list cells | Nested arrays, which must be rectangular |
| factor | 1-based integer indices in level order, plus `J_<name>`, the number of levels |
| string | Rejected, as in CmdStanR 1.0; make the column a factor so its levels set the codes |
| null, dates, other objects | Rejected with the column name and row, because Stan data has no missing values |

Factor levels come from a `toModelData()` descriptor (`['levels' => list<string>, 'codes' => list<?int>, 'ordered' => bool]`, with 0-based codes, as phibble's `DataFrame::toModelData()` returns them from phibble 0.1.0; add `'base' => 1` for 1-based codes) or, for a `toColumns()` table, from `levels($name)` when `types()` reports a factor. The `ordered` flag is ignored. Labels cannot be written to Stan JSON, so they are returned in `StanData::$levels`, keyed by data variable, where label `i` has index `i + 1`. The conversion adds `N`, the row count, unless the table has a column named `N`, and adds `J_<name>` unless a column already has that name. CmdStan ignores data variables that the program does not declare. Column names must be valid Stan identifiers.

Fit methods are camelCase, as are `StanData`'s and `Tables`' `from...()` constructors and the package's other static helpers, such as `CmdStanFit::fromCsv()` and `Inits::fromFit()`. `StanData` is a value object with readonly `data`, `levels`, `columns` (the names of the columns of `X`), and `meta`. `toArray()` returns `data`, and `with(['prior_scale' => 2.5])` adds or replaces variables.

### Regression data

`StanData::fromColumns($columns, y: 'y', x: ['x1', 'x2'], groups: 'school', intercept: false)` builds the usual hierarchical regression data block from named columns or a table:

| Variable | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `N` | Number of rows |
| `K` | Number of predictors (columns of `X`) |
| `X` | N rows of K floats, in the order of `x` |
| `y` | The outcome, keeping integers as integers |
| `<g>_id` | For each grouping column `g`, the 1-based group index of each row |
| `J_<g>` | For each grouping column, the number of groups |
| `J` | The number of groups, when there is exactly one grouping column |

Groups are numbered over sorted unique values (numbers numerically, otherwise in `strcmp` order) or over a factor's levels, and the labels are in `levels['<g>_id']`. Predictors must be numeric. `intercept: true` prepends a column of ones named `(Intercept)`. It is off by default because Stan programs usually give the intercept its own parameter.

```php
$data = CmdStan\StanData::fromColumns($df, 'score', ['hours'], 'school');
$fit = $model->sample(data: $data, seed: 1);
```

```stan
data {
  int<lower=0> N;
  int<lower=0> K;
  matrix[N, K] X;
  vector[N] y;
  int<lower=1> J;
  array[N] int<lower=1, upper=J> school_id;
}
```

`StanData::fromFormula('y ~ x1 + f + (1 + x1 | g)', $data, dropIntercept: false, missing: 'drop')` builds regression data from an R-style formula through `Phit\model_matrix()` in the [`phit`](https://github.com/phpstats/phit) extension (phit 0.1.0 and later). The function handles factor predictors (treatment contrasts), interactions, transforms, and offsets, and keeps the `(Intercept)` column in `X` unless `dropIntercept: true`. `$data` can be columns, factor descriptors, or a table, whose `toModelData()` is passed unchanged. Without the function, `fromFormula()` throws a `RuntimeException` that names the requirement. `StanData::fromModelMatrix($result)` maps an existing `Phit\model_matrix()` result and is the only code that depends on its shape.

| Formula part | Stan data |
| --- | --- |
| Design matrix | `N` (retained rows), `K`, and `X`; the column names are in `columns` |
| Numeric response | `y`, as integers when every value is integral, so it suits `int` and `real` declarations |
| Factor response | `y` as 0/1 for two levels (Bernoulli), or 1..`C` with `C` levels (categorical); labels in `levels['y']` |
| `cbind(s, f)` response | `y` (successes) and `trials` (successes plus failures) |
| `offset()` | `offset` |
| `(... \| g)` | `<g>_id` (1-based) and `J_<g>` per grouping factor, and `J` when there is one grouping factor |
| Random slopes, such as `(1 + x \| g)` | `Z_<g>` (N rows of the group's columns, including the intercept column) and `Q_<g>`, the number of columns; omitted when every term on the group is intercept-only |

Group names that are not Stan identifiers have other characters replaced by `_`, so the nested group `g2:g1` gives `g2_g1_id`. Groups are numbered in factor level order when the data has descriptors or table factors, and otherwise over sorted labels (numbers numerically, otherwise byte order, as `Phit\model_matrix()` sorts levels). Terms on the same group are concatenated into one `Z_<g>`, intercept-only terms included, so `(1 | g) + (0 + x | g)` gives the same `Z_g` as `(1 + x | g)`. Two groups whose names map to the same `<g>`, such as `a.b` and `a_b`, are rejected. Factors reach `Phit\model_matrix()` as descriptors in the data's level order, so the first level is the reference level and a factor response is coded in that order, while plain string columns use sorted levels. `missing: 'drop'` removes rows with missing values in any variable the formula uses, with one `E_WARNING` from `Phit\model_matrix()`, and `missing: 'raise'` rejects them. The remaining result keys, including `retained_rows`, `dropped_rows`, `n_input`, `n_dropped`, `terms`, and `assign`, are kept in `meta`, and `meta['random'][<g>]` lists each group's columns and terms.

```stan
data {
  int<lower=0> N;
  int<lower=1> K;
  matrix[N, K] X;          // includes the intercept column
  vector[N] y;
  int<lower=1> J;
  array[N] int<lower=1, upper=J> g_id;
  int<lower=1> Q_g;
  matrix[N, Q_g] Z_g;      // (1 + x1 | g)
}
```

### Draws and summaries out

- `drawsColumns(variables: null, incWarmup: false)` returns draws as columns, like posterior's `as_draws_df()`: one list per variable element (such as `beta[2]`), then one-based `.chain`, `.iteration`, and `.draw` columns.
- `summaryColumns(variables: null, probs: [0.05, 0.95], measures: [])` returns `summary()` as columns: `variable` and one column per measure.
- `drawsTable()` and `summaryTable()` take the same arguments and return a `Phibble\DataFrame` built with `DataFrame::fromColumns()`. They need `phpstats/phibble`, which requires PHP 8.3 or later, and throw a `RuntimeException` explaining this when it is not installed.
- `CmdStan\Tables::fromRows($rows)` converts any list of associative rows, such as `loo()['pointwise']`, to columns.

The column arrays need no other package and suit any data frame library that accepts name-to-values columns.

### Part of the phpstats family

CmdStanPHP is part of the phpstats family of PHP statistics packages:

- [phit](https://github.com/phpstats/phit): the `phit` native extension (`Phit\` functions), which provides the moment-matching draw kernels and, when available, `Phit\model_matrix()`.
- [phibble](https://github.com/phpstats/phibble): data frames (`Phibble\DataFrame`).
- [phplyr](https://github.com/phpstats/phplyr): dplyr-style verbs for phibble tables.
- [phiz](https://github.com/phpstats/phiz): a Vega-Lite grammar of graphics.

CmdStanPHP requires none of them. phibble, phplyr, and phiz require PHP 8.3 or later, and the phit extension supports PHP 8.3, 8.4, and 8.5.

## Errors

| Exception | Thrown when |
| --- | --- |
| `InvalidArgumentException` | Data or options are invalid |
| `RuntimeException` | Files or the toolchain are missing, a process times out, or a CSV file is malformed |
| `StaleExecutableException` | The executable is out of date |
| `ProcessException` | A CmdStan process exits with a nonzero status. Its readonly properties are `command`, `exitCode`, `stdout`, and `stderr`. |

`StaleExecutableException` and `ProcessException` extend `RuntimeException`. A failing chain stops the other running chains, and its partial output files stay on disk for inspection. Partial output is never returned as a successful fit. CmdStan processes still running when PHP shuts down are terminated.
